context:
Create a convenience script or CLI subcommand that:
1. Runs the same benchmark (e.g., TPC-H SF=1) on both pg_duckdb and duckdb
2. Feeds both result files to PlatformComparison.from_files() which already
   handles Welch's t-test, Bonferroni correction, and win/loss matrix
3. Formats the ComparisonReport with pg_duckdb-specific annotations:
   overhead percentage per query, geometric mean overhead, queries where
   pg_duckdb wins (if any)

The comparison infrastructure already exists and is mature - this is
primarily an orchestration and formatting task. PlatformComparison
validates same benchmark name and scale factor, computes per-query
p50/p95/p99, and ranks via PlatformRanker with GEOMETRIC_MEAN strategy.

The script should also work with pre-existing result files (not just
live runs) so users can compare without re-running benchmarks.
description:
pg_duckdb embeds DuckDB inside PostgreSQL. A key user question is: what
overhead does the PostgreSQL integration layer add? BenchBox can already
run the same benchmark on both pg_duckdb and native DuckDB separately, but
there's no automated workflow to run both and generate a structured
comparison showing per-query timing deltas, overhead percentages, and
statistical significance.

This builds on the existing PlatformComparison infrastructure in
benchbox/core/analysis/comparison.py rather than creating new comparison
logic.

Split from pg-extension-advanced-benchmarking (originally deferred from
pg-duckdb-platform-adapter, completed 2026-02-15).

anti_patterns.why: PlatformComparison already handles statistical tests, win/loss, and ranking

anti_patterns.dont: require live database connections for comparison
anti_patterns.instead: accept result file paths as input
anti_patterns.why: users may want to compare pre-existing result files

preserves.behavior: Existing pg_duckdb and duckdb adapter behavior unmodified
PlatformComparison and PlatformRanker APIs unchanged - consume, don't modify

verifications.description: Comparison script runs with pre-existing result files

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/core/ -v -k analysis

work_units.summary: Create comparison script that orchestrates dual-platform runs and feeds results to PlatformComparison
Add overhead-specific formatting - per-query overhead %, geometric mean overhead, winner annotations
